paras.text: 3. Ligand

paras.text: The atoms, ions, or neutral molecules, which surrounds the central metal ion and donate electron pairs to it, are called ligands. They may be anions or neutral molecules. For example, K₄[Fe(CN)₆], [Ag(NH₃)₂]Cl. In these examples, the CN⁻ is anionic and NH₃ is the neutral ligand.

paras.text: i. Monodentate or Unidentate Ligands

paras.text: The ligands which possess only one donor site are called monodentate or unidentate ligands. Some examples are CN⁻, F⁻, Cl⁻, OH⁻, CO, NH₃, H₂O etc.

paras.text: ii. Multidentate or Polydentate Ligands

paras.pashto: ii. څو غاښیز لېګنډونه

paras.text: The ligands, which possess more than one donor sites are called multidentate, or polydentate ligands. Depending on the number of coordinating donor atoms, these are called bidentate (two), tridentate (three), tetradentate (four), pentadentate(five) and hexadentate (six) ligands. For example, ethylene diamine tetra acetic acid EDTA is an important hexadentate ligand.

paras.text: It refers to the total number of coordinate covalent bonds formed by the central metal ion with the ligands. paras.pashto: د کمپلېکس مرکباتو منظم نومونه د خالصې او تطبیقي کیمیا د نړیوالې ټولنې (IUPAC) د غیر عضوي نوم اېښودنې د کمېټې پر سپارښتل شوو اصولو ولاړ دي. د کواردینېشن مرکباتو د نوم اېښودنې اصول دا دي:

paras.text: 1. The cation is named before the anion, as in other ionic compounds. For example, in the K₃[Fe(CN)₆] and [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]Cl compounds, we name the K⁺ and [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ cations first, respectively.

paras.text: 2. In naming the complex ion, the ligand names are written in alphabetical order, before the name of the central metal ion. There should be no space between the name of the ligand and the name of the central metal ion.
paras.urdu: 2. کمپلیکس آئن کے نام میں لیگنڈز کے نام حروف تہجی کی ترتیب سے مرکزی دھاتی آئن کے نام سے پہلے لکھتے ہیں۔ لیگنڈ اور مرکزی دھاتی آئن کے ناموں کے درمیان خلا نہیں ہونا چاہیے۔
paras.pashto: 2. د کمپلېکس ایون په نوم اېښودنه کې د لېګنډونو نومونه په الفبايي ترتیب د مرکزي فلزي ایون له نوم څخه مخکې لیکل کېږي. د لېګنډ او مرکزي فلزي ایون د نومونو ترمنځ باید واټن نه وي.

paras.text: 3. Numerical prefixes di, tri, tetra etc., are used for indicating the number of the same kind of ligand. Thus, the ligands in the cation [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ are “tetraamminedichloro”. If the ligand already contains a Greek prefix (e.g. ethylendiamine) if it is polydentate ligands the prefixes, bis-, tris-, tetrakis-, pentakis- are used instead. Numerical prefixes are not considered for determination of alphabetical order.

3. Ligand

The atoms, ions, or neutral molecules, which surrounds the central metal ion and donate electron pairs to it, are called ligands. They may be anions or neutral molecules. For example, K₄[Fe(CN)₆], [Ag(NH₃)₂]Cl. In these examples, the CN⁻ is anionic and NH₃ is the neutral ligand.

Depending upon the number of donor atoms (or site), the ligands may be classified into various categories as follows.

i. Monodentate or Unidentate Ligands

The ligands which possess only one donor site are called monodentate or unidentate ligands. Some examples are CN⁻, F⁻, Cl⁻, OH⁻, CO, NH₃, H₂O etc.

ii. Multidentate or Polydentate Ligands

The ligands, which possess more than one donor sites are called multidentate, or polydentate ligands. Depending on the number of coordinating donor atoms, these are called bidentate (two), tridentate (three), tetradentate (four), pentadentate(five) and hexadentate (six) ligands. For example, ethylene diamine tetra acetic acid EDTA is an important hexadentate ligand.

4. Coordination Number

It refers to the total number of coordinate covalent bonds formed by the central metal ion with the ligands. For example, in [CoCl₂(NH₃)₄]Cl, [Cu(NH₃)₆]Cl₂, K₃[Cr(C₂O₄)₃] and K₄[Fe(CN)₆], six coordinate covalent bonds are formed between the ligands and the central metal ion and the coordination number is six, while in [Cu(NH₃)₄]SO₄, four coordinate covalent bonds are in between the ligand NH₃ and the central metal ion and the coordination number is four.

5. Coordination Sphere

The central atom along with the surrounding ligands are enclosed in a square bracket and forms coordination sphere. It may be anionic, cationic or neutral. For example, K₄[Fe(CN)₆], [Cu(NH₃)₄]SO₄ and [Ni(CO)₄]. In these examples, [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻, [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺, and [Ni(CO)₄]⁰ are an ionic, cationic and neutral coordination sphere respectively and K⁺ and SO₄²⁻ are the ionization sphere.

The part present outside the bracket is called ionization sphere as it is ionisable in solution.

6. Charge on the Coordination Sphere

It is the algebraic sum of the charges present on the central metal ion and the total charge on the ligands. For example, [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻

Charge on iron, Fe = +2

Total charge on six CN⁻ ions = −6

Charge on the Coordination Sphere = −6 + 2 = −4

7. Chelates

The bonding of a polydentate ligand to a metal ion through more than one site is called chelating ligand. These ligands produce a ring like structure called chelate. The polydentate ligand is called a chelating agent, the process of chelate formation is called chelation and the compounds formed are known as chelate compounds. Chelation increases the stability of complex. For example, ethylene diamide acts as a bidentate chelating ligand.

14.2.2 Nomenclature of Coordination Compounds

The systematic names of complex compounds are based on rules recommended by the Inorganic Nomenclature Committee of International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC). The rules for naming the coordination compounds are as follows:

1. دوسرے آئنک مرکبات کی طرح مثبت آئن کا نام منفی آئن سے پہلے ہے۔ مثلاً K₃[Fe(CN)₆] اور [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]Cl میں بالترتیب K⁺ اور [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ مثبت آئنوں کے نام پہلے ہیں۔

2. کمپلیکس آئن کے نام میں لیگنڈز کے نام حروف تہجی کی ترتیب سے مرکزی دھاتی آئن کے نام سے پہلے لکھتے ہیں۔ لیگنڈ اور مرکزی دھاتی آئن کے ناموں کے درمیان خلا نہیں ہونا چاہیے۔

3. ایک ہی قسم کے لیگنڈ کی تعداد کے لیے di، tri، tetra وغیرہ عددی سابقے ہیں۔ یوں [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ کے لیگنڈز tetraamminedichloro ہیں۔ اگر لیگنڈ میں پہلے یونانی سابقہ ہو (مثلاً ethylendiamine)، یا کثیر دندانی لیگنڈ ہو، تو bis-، tris-، tetrakis- اور pentakis- استعمال کرتے ہیں۔ حروف تہجی کی ترتیب مقرر کرنے میں عددی سابقے شمار نہیں ہوتے۔

3. Ligand

The atoms, ions, or neutral molecules, which surrounds the central metal ion and donate electron pairs to it, are called ligands. They may be anions or neutral molecules. For example, K₄[Fe(CN)₆], [Ag(NH₃)₂]Cl. In these examples, the CN⁻ is anionic and NH₃ is the neutral ligand.

Depending upon the number of donor atoms (or site), the ligands may be classified into various categories as follows.

i. Monodentate or Unidentate Ligands

The ligands which possess only one donor site are called monodentate or unidentate ligands. Some examples are CN⁻, F⁻, Cl⁻, OH⁻, CO, NH₃, H₂O etc.

ii. Multidentate or Polydentate Ligands

The ligands, which possess more than one donor sites are called multidentate, or polydentate ligands. Depending on the number of coordinating donor atoms, these are called bidentate (two), tridentate (three), tetradentate (four), pentadentate(five) and hexadentate (six) ligands. For example, ethylene diamine tetra acetic acid EDTA is an important hexadentate ligand.

4. Coordination Number

It refers to the total number of coordinate covalent bonds formed by the central metal ion with the ligands. For example, in [CoCl₂(NH₃)₄]Cl, [Cu(NH₃)₆]Cl₂, K₃[Cr(C₂O₄)₃] and K₄[Fe(CN)₆], six coordinate covalent bonds are formed between the ligands and the central metal ion and the coordination number is six, while in [Cu(NH₃)₄]SO₄, four coordinate covalent bonds are in between the ligand NH₃ and the central metal ion and the coordination number is four.

5. Coordination Sphere

The central atom along with the surrounding ligands are enclosed in a square bracket and forms coordination sphere. It may be anionic, cationic or neutral. For example, K₄[Fe(CN)₆], [Cu(NH₃)₄]SO₄ and [Ni(CO)₄]. In these examples, [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻, [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺, and [Ni(CO)₄]⁰ are an ionic, cationic and neutral coordination sphere respectively and K⁺ and SO₄²⁻ are the ionization sphere.

Figure 14.2 Coordination sphere.

The part present outside the bracket is called ionization sphere as it is ionisable in solution.

6. Charge on the Coordination Sphere

It is the algebraic sum of the charges present on the central metal ion and the total charge on the ligands. For example, [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻

Charge on iron, Fe = +2

Total charge on six CN⁻ ions = −6

Charge on the Coordination Sphere = −6 + 2 = −4

7. Chelates

The bonding of a polydentate ligand to a metal ion through more than one site is called chelating ligand. These ligands produce a ring like structure called chelate. The polydentate ligand is called a chelating agent, the process of chelate formation is called chelation and the compounds formed are known as chelate compounds. Chelation increases the stability of complex. For example, ethylene diamide acts as a bidentate chelating ligand.

14.2.2 Nomenclature of Coordination Compounds

The systematic names of complex compounds are based on rules recommended by the Inorganic Nomenclature Committee of International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC). The rules for naming the coordination compounds are as follows:

1. The cation is named before the anion, as in other ionic compounds. For example, in the K₃[Fe(CN)₆] and [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]Cl compounds, we name the K⁺ and [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ cations first, respectively.

2. In naming the complex ion, the ligand names are written in alphabetical order, before the name of the central metal ion. There should be no space between the name of the ligand and the name of the central metal ion.

3. Numerical prefixes di, tri, tetra etc., are used for indicating the number of the same kind of ligand. Thus, the ligands in the cation [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ are “tetraamminedichloro”. If the ligand already contains a Greek prefix (e.g. ethylendiamine) if it is polydentate ligands the prefixes, bis-, tris-, tetrakis-, pentakis- are used instead. Numerical prefixes are not considered for determination of alphabetical order.
